_why: A registry that only ENUMERATES cannot notice something missing. all_checks() returns whatever decorators happened to run, so one lost @check line removes a check while the verdict still reads 'healthy - all checks passing'. Demonstrated: deleting the decorator on rb_workflows_never_succeed dropped rb_wf_starved and changed nothing else about the output. This file is the REQUIRED set; w_checks_complete compares it against what actually ran and fails critically on a gap.
_adding_a_check: Add its id here in the same commit. Ids that run but are not listed are reported as 'unlisted' WITHOUT failing, so a new check never breaks the loop before you catch up. Classify it in the kinds map too - an unclassified id is reported by w_freshness_paired without failing.
_removing_a_check: Delete its id here deliberately, in a commit that says why. Retiring a check should be a decision with a diff, not an accident.
_kinds_why: R2 (ran is not worked) enforced mechanically: w_freshness_paired reads this map and fails, at warn, any domain that has run-status coverage but no output-freshness coverage. Classifying a new check here is one line; the five-day rappterbook silence is what it costs not to.
_unpaired_accepted_why: An accepted pairing gap is a DECISION with a diff, not a silence. A permanently-red pairing check would hold the verdict at degraded forever, which silently disables the level-3 evolve arm (sentinel only evolves while healthy) and trains readers to scroll past the channel. Each entry names the domain and why its gap is accepted; deleting an entry re-arms the check for that domain.

unpaired_accepted.ecosystem: the generic sweep's repos have no single output artifact to stamp; per-repo freshness bars are an owner decision, recorded as the eco_sweep row of CHECK-AUDIT.md (2026-08-16)
